newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung tops post-97 leadership popularity poll.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung tops post-97 leadership popularity poll.

text.p: Hong Kong's Tung Chee-hwa, viewed as favourite in the contest to govern the territory after the British leave in 1997, has a big lead over his nearest rival in popularity, a poll showed on Thursday.

The survey by the University of Hong Kong found 46.7 percent supported shipping tycoon Tung, while former chief judge Ti Liang Yang came second with just 28.8 percent and businessman Peter Woo was third with 5.2 percent.
This was how the respondents, a sample of 565 people polled by telephone on Monday, said they would vote if they could.
But the future chief executive, taking over from Governor Chris Patten, is to be picked by an elite 400-member Selection Committee under China's close scrutiny next Wednesday.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China at midnight next June 30, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.
